{{Top}}
{{Quote|Set S-foils into attack position.|[[Davijaan/Legends|Davijaan]]|<ref name="Episode 3">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
[[File:S-foils_blueprint.jpg|thumb|300px|X-wing starfighter s-foil blueprints.]]
'''S-foils''', also known as '''swing-wings''',<ref name="HSCSS">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref> '''strike foils''', '''stability foils''', '''stabilizer foils'''<ref name="MC">{{JournalCite|7|Missed Chance}}</ref> '''starfoils'''<ref name="IAG">''[[Introductory Adventure Game]]''</ref> and, on occasion, as '''X-foils''',<ref name="A Guide to the Star Wars Universe">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> were movable wings attached to the port and starboard sides of a starship, sometimes mounted with weaponry. Normally, the foils were locked in a "closed" position close to the ship for landing and usually for normal flight, but during high-stress situations, the foils were folded out. The [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]] manufactured several [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] with S-foils, including the [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170 starfighter]] and, later, the [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]].

==Uses==
===Heat dispersion===
[[File:ARC_Fighters.png|thumb|left|250px|A squadron of [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170 fighters]] and [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class interceptors]] at the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]]. Both ships utilized S-foils to disperse engine heat.]]
Historically, S-foils had been developed to address overheating issues on wing-based starfighters. Because of the proximity of engines and weapons systems to narrow wiring that fit inside the thin wings, an excess of heat could cause mechanical meltdowns that would be devastating to the fighters' capacity to function. S-foils like those seen on a number of Republic starfighter models during the Clone Wars held radiator panels that dispersed heat and cooled the ships' interior mechanisms. S-foils were used when stress was being put on a ship's systems, usually when it was traveling at high speeds or locked in a dogfight. This idea would eventually evolve into the radiator panels of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]].

===Atmospheric stabilization===
Stabilization was a key issue, especially with larger craft. For shuttles, which were often used to transport dignitaries or sensitive cargo, maintaining stability in flight was pivotal. Large folding wings served to reduce turbulence and protect the craft's contents.

===Weapon range===
[[File:BwingStarfighter-BaseSeries4.png|thumb|180px|A [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing starfighter]] in the process of extending its S-foils for combat.]]
With the advent of newer starfighters like [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom's]] [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]], the workhorse of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], S-foils took on a new purpose. Designers realized that they could increase spread coverage of weapons if they mounted them at the tips of the foils. Unfortunately, the new design had the side effect of decreasing the reaction time of patrol fighters. On most models with S-foil mounted laser cannons, the weapons could not fire with the foils in locked position. As such, a pilot would have to switch to attack mode before they could defend themselves. Even in fighters where that was not the case, accuracy was usually improved with the S-foils in attack position.
